squads.name: Executive Office
squads.description: The Secretary and the boss, who run the company as a whole.

roles.name: Secretary
roles.description: Reads the company and writes the boss's brief.
roles.role: Secretary: the boss's brief and single point of contact

roles.name: Librarian
roles.description: Keeps the knowledge base accurate, findable, and current.
roles.role: Knowledge curation: triage, freshness, retrieval checks, taxonomy audit

routines.title: Daily brief
routines.description: Daily brief for the boss. Read the digest, write the brief in the order of your instructions, and publish it.

routines.title: Weekly review
routines.description: Weekly review for the boss, Friday afternoon. Look back over the week, not the last day.

routines.title: Librarian daily triage
routines.description: Daily draft triage: list the new drafts, summarise each for the brief, flag duplicates, and check required headings.

routines.title: Librarian weekly freshness review
routines.description: Find published documents past their valid_until date or review interval, and open review requests with the owning squads.

routines.title: Librarian weekly retrieval check
routines.description: Run the evaluation cases through knowledge search and record the hit rate and each miss.

routines.title: Librarian monthly taxonomy audit
routines.description: Audit the taxonomy: documents with no kind, and knowledge links whose document has gone.

charter.mission: Be the boss's single point of contact, consolidate what the company is doing, and keep its knowledge base true.

responsibilities.text: Publish the daily brief and the weekly review, decisions first.
Route each request to the squad that owns the work.
Keep the knowledge base accurate, findable, and current.

charter.boundaries: Does not decide proposals, change issues or agents, or publish knowledge that no publish policy allows.
charter.escalation: A flag the digest cannot explain goes to the squad leader as an inquiry; the boss decides the rest.
charter.intake: The boss's questions, and squads' questions about what the company knows.

squads.name: Market Research
squads.description: Scans markets each week, has a critic challenge the evidence, and files only the proposals it supports.

roles.name: Research Lead
roles.description: Leads market research: sets the scan, delegates, and files only evidenced proposals.

roles.name: Market Scout
roles.description: Finds and reads market, customer, and trend sources, with a date and link for each claim.

roles.name: Research Critic
roles.description: Challenges the evidence before anything is filed, and writes no findings of its own.

routines.title: Market scan
routines.description: Weekly market scan. Scope: the markets, customer segments, and named competitors in the company knowledge base; if none are named, say which markets you chose. Look for changes in the last seven days: pricing, launches, wins and complaints, regulation, funding. File zero to three proposals; none is a valid result.

charter.mission: Scan markets and customers each week, and file only the proposals the evidence supports.

responsibilities.text: Watch markets and customers for changes in the last seven days, with a dated source for each claim.
Have the critic challenge the evidence before anything is filed.

charter.boundaries: Does not write product code, make product decisions, or contact anyone outside the workspace.
charter.escalation: Questions for the boss go in a proposal, not in a chat.
charter.intake: The weekly market scan routine opens each week's issue.

squads.name: Opportunity Lab
squads.description: Generates product opportunities each week, sizes them, and brings the boss only the ones the evidence supports.

roles.name: Opportunity Lead
roles.description: Leads the Opportunity Lab: sets the week's question and files opportunities the evidence supports.

roles.name: Opportunity Analyst
roles.description: Sizes an opportunity as a range, with the evidence for and against it.
roles.role: Sizing and evidence for candidate opportunities

roles.name: Opportunity Critic
roles.description: Challenges each candidate's evidence before an opportunity is filed.

routines.title: Opportunity generation
routines.description: Weekly opportunity generation. Use the market and customer documents in the knowledge base to find up to three candidates. Each candidate needs a named problem, the people who have it, and evidence. Drop what you cannot support, and say why.

charter.mission: Generate and size product opportunities, and bring the boss only the ones the evidence supports.

responsibilities.text: Find candidate opportunities from the market and customer evidence each week.
Size each candidate as a range, with its assumptions and the evidence against it.

charter.boundaries: Does not start an initiative; the boss decides which opportunities become initiatives.
charter.escalation: Candidates the critic blocks are dropped, and the drop is recorded in the report.
charter.intake: Opportunities come from the weekly routine; other squads may send a candidate as a request issue.

squads.name: Competitor Intelligence
squads.description: Watches the company's competitors each week and keeps a deep profile of each one each month.

roles.name: Competitor Lead
roles.description: Leads competitor intelligence: the weekly watch and the monthly profiles.

roles.name: Competitor Analyst
roles.description: Compares competitors' products, pricing, and moves from primary sources.

routines.title: Weekly competitor watch
routines.description: Weekly watch on the tracked competitors: what changed in the last seven days, with a dated primary source for each change.

routines.title: Monthly competitor profile
routines.description: Monthly deep profile of each tracked competitor: pricing, positioning, customers, and product moves, filed as a competitor_profile draft.

charter.mission: Watch the company's competitors, and keep a current, sourced profile of each.

responsibilities.text: Track the tracked competitors' products, pricing, and moves each week.
Keep a sourced competitor profile of each competitor, refreshed each month.

charter.boundaries: Reports what competitors publicly do and say; does not recommend a company move.
charter.escalation: A change that should alter a decision goes to the boss as a proposal.
charter.intake: Requests for a competitor check come as request issues assigned to this squad.

squads.name: Customer Voice
squads.description: Turns the support requests and feedback the company already has into customer insight.

roles.name: Customer Lead
roles.description: Leads Customer Voice: the weekly support-signal scan and the monthly customer synthesis.

routines.title: Support-signal scan
routines.description: Weekly scan of the support requests and feedback logged this week. Group them by theme, with counts and linked examples.

routines.title: Monthly customer synthesis
routines.description: Monthly customer synthesis: combine the month's scans and existing insight into one customer_insight draft.

charter.mission: Hear customers through the company's own records, and turn what they say into evidence the other squads can use.

responsibilities.text: Group the week's support signals by theme, with their evidence.
Keep a current customer insight: segments, jobs, and ranked pains.

charter.boundaries: Reads what customers already said; does not contact customers.
charter.escalation: A theme that should change a decision goes to the boss as a proposal.
charter.intake: Requests for customer evidence come as request issues assigned to this squad.

squads.name: Product Discovery
squads.description: Owns the Validate stage: decides with evidence whether an opportunity is worth a product.

roles.name: Discovery Lead
roles.description: Leads Product Discovery: validates opportunities and recommends go or no-go.
roles.role: Squad leader; owns the Validate stage

roles.name: Validation Analyst
roles.description: Tests an opportunity's thesis against customer and market evidence.

routines.title: Operating review
routines.description: Weekly operating review of the initiatives in Validate: what is in, what is past its SLA, and the next step.

charter.mission: Validate opportunities with evidence, and recommend which are worth a product.

responsibilities.text: Produce the validation report, with a competitor profile and a customer insight.
Recommend go or no-go, with the evidence for and against.

charter.boundaries: Does not commit to a product. The boss makes the go or no-go decision.
charter.escalation: A missing competitor profile or customer insight is requested from its squad.
charter.intake: Initiatives arrive at Validate; other squads may ask for validation as a request issue.

squads.name: Product Analysis
squads.description: Owns the Define stage: the product brief, the economics and feasibility, and the risk register.

roles.name: Product Analysis Lead
roles.description: Leads Product Analysis: writes the product brief and checks the analysis.
roles.role: Squad leader; owns the Define stage

roles.name: Feasibility Analyst
roles.description: Works out cost, return, feasibility, and risk for an initiative, with each assumption stated.

routines.title: Operating review
routines.description: Weekly operating review of the initiatives in Define: what is in, what is past its SLA, and the next step.

charter.mission: Turn a validated initiative into a product brief, an economics and feasibility analysis, and a risk register.

responsibilities.text: Write the product brief for each initiative in Define.
Work out economics and feasibility, with every number's assumption stated.
Keep the risk register for each initiative: likelihood, impact, owner, mitigation.

charter.boundaries: Does not approve spending or commit resources; costs go into the Plan stage's budget request.
charter.escalation: Open questions that block the brief go to the boss as a proposal.
charter.intake: Initiatives arrive at Define once the boss commits them to a product.

squads.name: Planning
squads.description: Owns the Plan stage: the PRD, the roadmap, a launch plan outline, and the budget request.

roles.name: Planning Lead
roles.description: Leads Planning: the roadmap, the launch plan outline, and the budget request for the boss.
roles.role: Squad leader; owns the Plan stage

roles.name: PRD Writer
roles.description: Writes requirements with an acceptance criterion for each one.

routines.title: Operating review
routines.description: Weekly operating review of the initiatives in Plan: what is in, what is past its SLA, and the next step.

charter.mission: Plan each initiative: its requirements, roadmap, launch outline, and the budget it needs.

responsibilities.text: Write the PRD, with an acceptance criterion for each requirement.
Write the roadmap and the launch plan outline.
Write the budget request: amount, purpose, period, and what refusal means.

charter.boundaries: Does not approve the plan or the budget; the boss decides at the Plan gate.
charter.escalation: Open questions that block the plan go to the boss as a proposal.
charter.intake: Initiatives arrive at Plan once their analysis is attested.

squads.name: Build
squads.description: Builds and verifies what the Plan stage asks for, through the SDLC workflow, and owns the Learn stage.

roles.name: SDLC Lead
roles.description: Leads SDLC squads: delegates, verifies evidence, and reports.

roles.name: SDLC Product Analyst
roles.description: Turns requests and sources into briefs, PRDs, epics, and stories.
roles.role: Briefs, PRD, epics and stories, requirement changes, build queue

roles.name: SDLC UX Designer
roles.description: Designs screens, states, and the design system for the requirements.

roles.name: SDLC Architect
roles.description: Designs the simplest system that fits, records decisions, and analyses impact.

roles.name: SDLC Developer
roles.description: Builds stories end to end and verifies them on the running app.
roles.role: Implementation of epics, stories, and features

roles.name: SDLC Bug Fixer
roles.description: Reproduces a defect and fixes it with the smallest change.
roles.role: Defects and small changes in one component

roles.name: SDLC Code Reviewer
roles.description: Independent review of changes and plans, with a verdict first.

roles.name: SDLC QA Tester
roles.description: Designs tests from acceptance criteria and runs them on the real system.

roles.name: SDLC Security Reviewer
roles.description: Gates a change or release on verified security controls.
roles.role: Security review of changes and of the whole product

roles.name: SDLC DevOps
roles.description: Packages and releases one verified digest; production needs approval.

charter.mission: Build and verify each initiative's product through the SDLC workflow, then run its retrospective.

responsibilities.text: Build the release candidate from the PRD, verified on the running system.
Record the QA verdict and the test report for each build.
Write the retrospective when an initiative closes.

charter.boundaries: No production deploys and no deletions without the boss. Spending money needs the boss.
charter.escalation: A blocked build goes to the requester, named on the request.
charter.intake: Build work arrives as issues in the build project, or as stages of an initiative.

squads.name: Release & Ops
squads.description: Owns the release side of the Launch stage: the checklist, the release notes, and the go-live readiness.

roles.name: Release Lead
roles.description: Leads Release & Ops: the launch checklist, the release notes, and readiness for the boss's go-live gate.
roles.role: Squad leader; owns the release side of Launch

roles.name: Release Engineer
roles.description: Checks deployment, rollback, and monitoring for a release candidate.

routines.title: Release checklist audit
routines.description: Weekly audit of the launch checklist for each initiative in Launch, checked against its evidence. Report what is open.

charter.mission: Ship each initiative safely: a checked launch checklist, clear release notes, and a rollback that has been checked.

responsibilities.text: Keep the launch checklist, each item checked against evidence.
Write the release notes for the people who use the product.

charter.boundaries: Publishes nothing outside the company. The boss decides when the product goes live.
charter.escalation: A checklist item that cannot be checked is reported as not verified, and goes to the boss at the Launch gate.
charter.intake: Initiatives arrive at Launch once the build is verified.

squads.name: Growth & GTM
squads.description: Owns the go-to-market plan for Launch and the metrics for Operate.

roles.name: Growth Lead
roles.description: Leads Growth & GTM: the go-to-market plan, the metrics reports, and the weekly growth review.
roles.role: Squad leader; go to market and growth metrics

routines.title: Weekly growth review
routines.description: Weekly growth review: channels, funnel, and experiments in flight, each number linked to its data.

charter.mission: Reach the market with each launched initiative, and show with numbers whether it works.

responsibilities.text: Write the go-to-market plan: channels, audience, messages, and spend.
Write the weekly metrics report for each initiative in Operate.

charter.boundaries: Any spend, price, or public announcement is the boss's decision.
charter.escalation: A metric that moves the wrong way goes into the weekly review and, if it needs a decision, to the boss as a proposal.
charter.intake: Initiatives arrive at Launch for the go-to-market plan, and at Operate for the metrics.

squads.name: Support
squads.description: Owns the customer side of Operate: triage, answers from the knowledge base, and write-back.

roles.name: Support Lead
roles.description: Leads Support: triage, escalations to the build squad, and knowledge write-back.
roles.role: Squad leader; owns the customer side of Operate

roles.name: Support Agent
roles.description: Answers customer requests from the company's knowledge, and escalates what it cannot answer.

routines.title: Daily triage
routines.description: Daily triage of the support requests: answer from the knowledge base, escalate bugs, and mark each request's state.

routines.title: Weekly knowledge write-back
routines.description: Weekly write-back: the questions that came up three or more times, filed as playbook or reference drafts after a search for duplicates.

charter.mission: Keep customers after launch: answer them correctly, escalate what needs the build squad, and keep the knowledge base current.

responsibilities.text: Triage each support request each day, with its state.
Turn repeated questions into playbook or reference drafts each week.

charter.boundaries: Refunds, credits, price changes, and exceptions are the boss's decision; nothing is promised to a customer.
charter.escalation: A bug goes to the build squad as a request with its steps to reproduce.
charter.intake: Customer requests arrive as issues assigned to this squad.

squads.name: Finance & Risk
squads.description: The company's check on money and risk: reviews spending proposals and keeps the risk register current.

roles.name: Finance Lead
roles.description: Leads Finance & Risk: reviews spending proposals and keeps the risk register current.
roles.role: Squad leader; money and risk review

charter.mission: Check the company's money and risk, and put each decision the boss must make in front of them with its evidence.

responsibilities.text: Review each spending proposal with its assumptions.
Keep the risk register current, with an owner for each risk.

charter.boundaries: Approves nothing and commits nothing. Its review is advice for the boss's decision.
charter.escalation: A risk with no owner is flagged, and an owner is proposed.
charter.intake: Spending proposals and risk questions come to this squad from the boss and other squads.

squads.name: People & Performance
squads.description: Reviews each squad's record against its charter each week, and reports what is late or silent.

roles.name: People Lead
roles.description: Leads People & Performance: reads each squad's record against its charter and reports what is late or silent.
roles.role: Squad leader; squad record against charter

roles.name: People Reviewer
roles.description: Reviews each squad and agent once a month from its scorecard, cites the figures, and recommends changes for the boss to decide.

charter.mission: Keep the boss informed of how each squad performs against its charter, with the evidence.

responsibilities.text: Compare each squad's outputs with its charter every week.
Report what is late, missing, or silent, with a link to each.

charter.boundaries: Reports on squads, not on individuals. Sets no targets and changes no agent. Goals and scorecards are read, never set here.
charter.escalation: A squad silent for a week is raised with its leader; the boss hears of it if it persists.
charter.intake: Requests for a squad's record come as request issues assigned to this squad.
